title: Flat models and generators
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$ and $X$
a scheme of finite type over the standing field. Every $C\in\Dctf(X,A)$ on
$X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is represented by a bounded complex of flat constructible
$A$-sheaves. A flat constructible sheaf has a finite stratification on which
it is locally constant with finite projective $A$-module local models.
Consequently $\Dctf(X,A)$ is generated, using shifts, finite extensions and
direct summands, by sheaves $a_!L$, where $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is locally
closed and $L$ is locally constant with finite projective local models.

*Complement (generation over a Noetherian base).* More generally, let $X$ be a
Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Every object of
$\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ lies in the thick subcategory of $D(X,\Lambda)$ generated by
the objects $Rg_*j_!L$, where $U\subset X$ is a locally closed stratum of a
stratification of $X$, $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ is the open immersion
into its closure, $g:\overline U\hookrightarrow X$ is the closed immersion of
the closure, and $L$ is a lisse (finite locally constant) sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules on $U$ with flat stalks. That is, every property of objects
of $D(X,\Lambda)$ that is triangulated (contains $0$ and is stable under shifts
and under extensions in distinguished triangles), stable under retracts and
under isomorphisms, and holds for all these generators holds for every object
of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.

Conventions. The standing field is $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Work with ordinary module sheaves over the
constant finite ring on the small sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site;
def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and their derived categories
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In either site, $\Dctf$ means bounded
constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in some finite interval $[a,b]$:
$H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}M[0])=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ and every
$i\notin[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude; def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude].
Constructibility and lisse sheaves use
[def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf; def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf].
Flat means that tensoring with the sheaf is exact; a finite projective module
means a direct summand of a finite free module. A Noetherian scheme means a
quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Stratifications
are finite partitions by locally closed subschemes
[def-constructible-stratification]. For a locally closed immersion
$a:S\hookrightarrow X$, write $a_!L=g_*j_!L$ using its factorization through
its scheme-theoretic closure $S\xrightarrow{j}\overline S\xrightarrow{g}X$;
this fixes the locally closed extension-by-zero notation. The open
extension by zero is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] on the étale site and
[def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero] on the pro-étale site. The complement is
valid on either small site with these conventions.

proof.text: Finite type over the standing field makes X locally Noetherian, and quasi-compactness makes it Noetherian. Finite coefficient rings are Noetherian. These hypotheses allow the finite-value etale model and comparison interval theorem below. The Noetherian complement already assumes this hypothesis.

source.place: First paragraph and complement: Noetherian hypotheses

proof.text: Use finiteRing_constructibleDerived_origin for the specified intrinsic comparison functor to descend the bounded constructible object K to an etale object K0. Boundedness makes K0 bounded below. Choose the finite Tor interval of K, transport it across the comparison isomorphism and the derived composition isomorphism, and apply comparison_torAmplitudeIn_iff to obtain the same interval for K0. This uses the fixed comparison functor, not an arbitrarily chosen equivalence of categories.

source.place: First paragraph: comparison descent and Tor interval

proof.text: Apply hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_finiteValueConstructibleModel on the etale site. Apply finiteCoefficientIntrinsicComparison termwise to the resulting bounded complex. Its exactness preserves zero terms and the representing isomorphism via mapDerivedCategoryFactors. Flatness follows from flat_comparisonUpperStar_obj and intrinsicRealization_flat. For constructibility, use the fixed-module constructibility comparison, intrinsicRealization_restriction, and proEtaleModuleRestriction_constructible_iff. This proves proEtaleFlatModel.

source.place: First paragraph: transport of the bounded flat constructible model

proof.text: For proEtaleFlatStratification, the definition of intrinsic constructibility already provides a finite locally closed stratification, with locally constant restrictions and finite geometric stalks. Restrict the scalar action to fixed modules, using localConstancy_iff and finite_stalk_iff. Flatness is preserved under pullback and identified with fixed-module tensor flatness by intrinsic_flat_iff and the realization/restriction isomorphism. Choose a locally constant trivializing pro-etale covering and discard its empty members; it remains a quasi-compact pro-etale covering. Each nonempty member has a geometric point obtained from an algebraic closure of a residue field. The over-site fiber isomorphism identifies its constant local model with the original geometric stalk. The model is finite and flat, hence finitely presented and projective over the finite ring. Finally the fully faithful constant-scalar restriction functor lifts these trivializations to intrinsic module sheaves. Empty schemes allow the empty covering.

source.place: First paragraph: projective local models on strata

proof.text: For the bounded etale model P, its stupid tails have degreewise split exact sequences 0 → P≥q+1 → P≥q → Pq[-q] → 0. The maps are inclusion and projection in the retained degrees. Each degree is either an identity exact sequence or all zero, so these sequences yield distinguished triangles. Starting from the zero tail above the upper bound and inducting down to the lower bound expresses the model using its shifted terms and finitely many extensions. In Lean, HomotopyCategory.mem_subcategory_of_strictly_bounded applies precisely this bounded-complex induction to the inverse-image property under DerivedCategory.Qh. Its hypotheses follow from the zero terms of the model; DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso identifies the quotient image with the derived model. For each term, the etale finite sheaf filtration described next provides the required property from closure generators.

source.place: First paragraph and complement: stupid truncation triangles; Stacks derived.tex Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, applied to the displayed degreewise split sequences

proof.text: Retain the etale property proof: the ordered-stratification and extension-filtration clauses of FlatModelGeneration express each flat constructible term using locally closed extensions. The canonical toImage/imageι factorization identifies these factors with sfEtaleClosureGenerators. Finite stalks give finite generation on locally constant restrictions; inverse image preserves flatness. Short exact sheaf sequences give single-object triangles, and finite induction proves the property for each term. The bounded homotopy-category devissage theorem applied to the inverse-image property under Qh proves it for the model. quotientCompQhIso and the representing isomorphism then give it for the etale input. Only the etale clauses of FlatModelGeneration are used.

source.place: Complement: finite sheaf filtration, stupid tails, and canonical closure factors

proof.text: For proEtaleThickGeneration descend K and its Tor interval as above. Apply etaleThickGeneration to the inverse-image property under the exact derived intrinsic comparison. Every etale generator maps to a pro-etale generator: lisse origin supplies lissity, comparison and intrinsic realization preserve flatness, and comparison commutes with open extension by zero and closed direct image. Here the underlying underived comparison theorem isIso_lowerStarComparisonUpperStarBaseChange suffices, since the generator predicates are already degree-zero sheaves. Isomorphism and retract stability transport along the functor, and the descent isomorphism proves the property for K.

source.place: Complement: comparison transport of the etale property formulation

proof.text: For equality let E be the etale constructible finite-Tor property and Q the essential image of E under derived intrinsic comparison. The bounded-constructible comparison is fully faithful, hence so is its restriction to E. Q is triangulated. It is also retract-stable: lift a retract projector by full faithfulness, split this idempotent on the bounded etale object using the bounded t-structure splitting theorem, and use retract-stability of E. The comparison interval theorem and bounded-constructible essential-image criterion show every Q-object has the required intrinsic constructibility and Tor amplitude. Conversely every pro-etale closure generator belongs to Q: descend its lisse sheaf by proEtale_lisse_origin, reflect flatness through the faithful exact monoidal comparison, and obtain finite projective stalks. The etale thick-generation equality puts its canonical extension in E. Open-extension and closed-direct-image comparisons identify its intrinsic image with the original generator. Nonemptiness of the generator property follows using the zero sheaf and the identity stratification, also for the empty scheme and zero coefficient ring. Apply proEtaleThickGeneration to the thick envelope for one inclusion, and triangEnvelope_le_iff with Q for the reverse inclusion.

source.place: First paragraph: reverse containment, retracts, and thick-envelope equality

split_report.blueprint: Steps 1–3 realize paragraph 1 comparison and bounded flat constructible model, also for the Noetherian complement. Step 4 realizes ordered flat sheaf strata and open–closed dévissage through the existing detailed node. Step 5 gives the stupid-tail induction; steps 6–7 realize the complement generators and property formulation. The cautionary paragraphs about cohomology and constant coefficients are recorded in the report, not used as proof premises.

tool_uses.why: The current blueprint explicitly descends along comparison; this existing theorem supplies the general finite-ring equivalence and interval preservation, not an identification with non-finite condensed coefficients.
The bounded flat constructible model is precisely the current blueprint model input; its general finite-ring statement avoids the older coefficient-restricted unit interface.
Exact comparison inverse image carries the termwise model and its quasi-isomorphism to the pro-etale site; this is a generic site-comparison tool.
Flatness preservation is a separate generic constant-coefficient inverse-image theorem; exactness alone is not used to infer it.
Finite-ring constructible sheaf comparison separately preserves constructibility of each model term.
The generic factorization of a quasi-compact immersion identifies each stratum as open in its scheme-theoretic closure.
Only its exact closed direct-image assertion is used on the etale site in the closure-generator identification.
Its exact closed direct image applies on the pro-etale site after the Noetherian retrocompact-complement check.
The generic exact-functor theorem identifies the termwise closed pushforward with its right derived functor, without additional resolution hypotheses.

lean.statement: theorem proEtaleFlatModel (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) (hl : l.Prime) (hlp : l ≠ D.p) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (hA : ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (l ^ n) • (1 : A) = 0) (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory X A) (hbc : (∀ q : ℤ, IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf X A ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (proEtaleRingModules X (proEtaleConstantRing X A)) q).obj K)) ∧ ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (proEtaleRingModules X (proEtaleConstantRing X A)) q).obj K)) (hTor : HasFiniteProEtaleTorAmplitude X A K) : ∃ (P : CochainComplex (proEtaleRingModules X (proEtaleConstantRing X A)) ℤ) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero (P.X q)) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := ProEt.topology X) (R := proEtaleConstantRing X A) (P.X q)) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf X A (P.X q)) ∧ Nonempty (K ≅ (_root_.DerivedCategory.Q).obj P)
